First sentence: DI solves the problem of tight coupling by allowing components to be more loosely coupled. That makes sense because when you inject dependencies, you don't have to create them yourself, reducing the need for direct references.

Second sentence: It also promotes better testability since dependencies can be easily mocked or replaced during testing. This is important because you can swap real implementations with test doubles without changing the code, which makes unit testing more straightforward.

Third sentence: Additionally, DI supports better modularity and reusability of code, as components can be developed and tested independently. This leads to more maintainable and scalable applications because changes in one part don't affect others as much.
